classification.difficultyReason: Read exact coordinates from a supplied unit circle and use the relevant ratio or reference angle.

content.prompt:
The unit circle shown has exact values.
Use the unit circle to find the exact value of these trigonometric functions.

spec.description: Unshaded unit circle with twelve exact coordinate labels, arrowed axes, two distinguished radial families and four directed angles.
spec.mathematics: The circumference points are (cos θ, sin θ) at multiples of 30°. Orange distinguishes the 30°, 150°, 210° and 330° radial family; blue distinguishes the 60°, 120°, 240° and 300° family. Directed arcs run counterclockwise from the positive x-axis to 30°, 120°, 210° and 300°.
spec.answerVisibility: All coordinates and angle annotations are permanent supplied givens. No requested part answers are printed in the diagram.

answer.worked: At $0^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin 0^{\circ}=0$.
At $0^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos 0^{\circ}=1$.

At $0^{\circ}$, $(x,y)=(1,0)$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 0^{\circ}&=\frac01\\\tan 0^{\circ}&=0\end{align*}$$

$120^{\circ}$ is in quadrant II, where sine is positive.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 120^{\circ}&=\sin 60^{\circ}\\\sin 120^{\circ}&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{align*}$$

$120^{\circ}$ is in quadrant II, where cosine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 120^{\circ}&=-\cos 60^{\circ}\\\cos 120^{\circ}&=-\frac12\end{align*}$$

$120^{\circ}$ is in quadrant II, where tangent is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 120^{\circ}&=-\tan 60^{\circ}\\\tan 120^{\circ}&=-\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

$300^{\circ}$ is in quadrant IV, where sine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 300^{\circ}&=-\sin 60^{\circ}\\\sin 300^{\circ}&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{align*}$$

$300^{\circ}$ is in quadrant IV, where cosine is positive.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 300^{\circ}&=\cos 60^{\circ}\\\cos 300^{\circ}&=\frac12\end{align*}$$

$300^{\circ}$ is in quadrant IV, where tangent is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 300^{\circ}&=-\tan 60^{\circ}\\\tan 300^{\circ}&=-\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

$210^{\circ}$ is in quadrant III, where cosine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 210^{\circ}&=-\cos 30^{\circ}\\\cos 210^{\circ}&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{align*}$$

$240^{\circ}$ is in quadrant III, where sine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 240^{\circ}&=-\sin 60^{\circ}\\\sin 240^{\circ}&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{align*}$$

$150^{\circ}$ is in quadrant II, where tangent is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 150^{\circ}&=-\tan 30^{\circ}\\\tan 150^{\circ}&=-\frac1{\sqrt3}\end{align*}$$
At $60^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin 60^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
At $30^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\frac12\right)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos 30^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$240^{\circ}$ is in quadrant III, where tangent is positive.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 240^{\circ}&=\tan 60^{\circ}\\\tan 240^{\circ}&=\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

$150^{\circ}$ is in quadrant II, where cosine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\cos 150^{\circ}&=-\cos 30^{\circ}\\\cos 150^{\circ}&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{align*}$$
At $90^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $(0,1)$. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos 90^{\circ}=0$.
At $180^{\circ}$, the unit-circle point is $(-1,0)$. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin 180^{\circ}=0$.

$210^{\circ}$ is in quadrant III, where sine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\sin 210^{\circ}&=-\sin 30^{\circ}\\\sin 210^{\circ}&=-\frac12\end{align*}$$

$330^{\circ}$ is in quadrant IV, where tangent is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 330^{\circ}&=-\tan 30^{\circ}\\\tan 330^{\circ}&=-\frac1{\sqrt3}\end{align*}$$
At $270^{\circ}$, $(x,y)=(0,-1)$. Tangent is $\frac{y}{x}$, which would require division by zero. Therefore $\tan 270^{\circ}$ is undefined.
